caveats: The app-launch rule's platform feature flag (RULE:a-insulin-glucose-check-app-launch, changeset 022) ships enabled=false; it was switched on through the admin flag API on this instance to exercise scenarios 7/8, so whether Mayo sees the app-launch variant depends on the flag state in production.
Insulin was staged through the admin bolus debugger (MedicationAdministrationEvent path), not Mayo HL7 RAS; infusions were not exercised, only boluses.
Scheduled-rule evaluations were forced with the admin quartz trigger endpoint; the 2-hour anchoring was verified from the stored trigger (next_fire_time, repeat_interval), not by waiting two hours.
Changeset 245 ran as a no-op on this empty Mayo schema; its SQL was re-run by hand against seeded firings, which proves the predicate but not the production data volume or the lock_timeout behaviour.
MGH interval and Mayo citations remain open questions on the ticket; MGH keeps 1h/1h defaults and subcutaneous 2-hour alerts carry no citation, as the merged code intends.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: On the Mayo tenant a subcutaneous insulin bolus scheduled the glucose reminder every 120 minutes and fired with the 2-hour wording, an IV bolus kept the 60-minute schedule and hourly wording, and the app-launch variant alerted once subcutaneous insulin was over 2 hours old.
Negative: A glucose result 65 minutes after subcutaneous insulin kept the rule silent, app launch 90 minutes after subcutaneous insulin was silent, and the demo tenant still scheduled every 60 minutes with the hourly wording.
Red check: Swapping in the pre-fix classes made the same Mayo subcutaneous bolus schedule a 1-hour reminder and the app-launch rule alert at 90 minutes; restoring the shipped classes brought the 2-hour behaviour back.

Automation: Unit tests for all eight scenarios shipped with the change; e2e coverage of the Mayo schedule, wording and default-site path is proposed.
